title: How to hide cursor in Pages on Mac: manual workarounds and system wide solutions
metaTitle: How to hide cursor on Mac in Pages: manual and system fixes
description: Learn how to hide cursor on Mac while using Pages. Discover why there is no native setting and the best third-party tools to manage your mouse visibility.
targetKeyword: how to hide cursor on mac
intro: There is no native setting in Apple Pages or macOS to manually hide the cursor on demand. You can only hide the cursor by using third-party utilities or by moving it to the edge of your screen.
tldr: Pages for Mac does not include a feature to hide the mouse cursor.
macOS hides the cursor automatically during video playback or in specific full-screen modes.
Third-party apps like Cursorcerer allow you to toggle cursor visibility with a keyboard shortcut.
Moving your mouse to the edge of the display remains the simplest manual workaround.

blocks.text: Why Pages lacks a cursor hide setting

Apple Pages is a word processor designed for standard document creation. It relies on the macOS system for cursor management. The cursor is a core UI element for accessibility and navigation. Apple does not provide a way to turn it off because doing so would hinder basic interaction. If you are coming from a Windows environment, you might be looking for a setting that does not exist on macOS. Windows allows users to hide the cursor while typing. macOS does not have this feature. The system handles cursor visibility based on activity. For example, it hides the cursor when you watch a video in full screen. It does not hide the cursor while you type in a document.
Manual ways to hide your cursor

When you need the cursor out of the way, you can move it to the edge of your screen. This is the most reliable manual method. If you have multiple displays, move the cursor to the far corner of your primary screen. It will slide over to the secondary display. This keeps it off your main canvas. If you are recording your screen, this keeps the cursor out of your frame. Some users also use a secondary monitor just to park the cursor. Another option is to keep the cursor behind a floating window. Open a small window and place it in a corner. Move your cursor behind that window. It will disappear from your view.

If you need to hide the cursor frequently, you should use a utility like Cursorcerer. This app adds a system-wide toggle for your cursor. The default keyboard shortcut is ⌃ ⌥ K. This works in every app, including Pages. You can hide the cursor with one press. Press the keys again to bring it back. This is useful for presentations or screen recordings. Ensure you enable the option to show the cursor if it is moved. This prevents you from losing the cursor permanently. Remember that such tools require accessibility permissions. They inject into the window server level of macOS. Always download these tools from trusted sources. Check the developer website for compatibility with your macOS version.

Many users want to hide the cursor for clean screen recordings. The built-in macOS Screenshot toolbar does not offer a hide cursor option. You must use professional recording software. OBS Studio is a common choice for Mac users. It has a per-source setting to show or hide the cursor. You can toggle this for your display capture. This keeps your recording clean without needing to move the mouse. Post-recording editing is another approach. You can use video software to crop the cursor out. This is time-consuming and often unnecessary. It is better to use software that controls the cursor during the capture phase.

items: Searching for hide cursor while typing in System Settings. This is not a Mac feature.
Forgetting to enable the show cursor on move setting in third-party apps.
Assuming full screen mode in Pages hides the cursor. It does not.
Using the wrong shortcut for third-party tools. Check your settings.

blocks.text: If your cursor seems stuck or invisible, check your third-party settings. If you are not using any tools, restart your Mac. Sometimes the system UI hangs. A restart refreshes the window server. Ensure your macOS is up to date. Apple frequently patches UI behavior in system updates. If you still have issues, check the Apple support forums. Many users share their experiences with cursor glitches there. Do not try to modify system files to hide the cursor. This can cause instability in your macOS installation.

faq.question: Can I hide the cursor in Pages using a native setting?
faq.answer: No. Apple Pages does not have a native setting to hide the mouse cursor.

faq.question: How do I hide the cursor for screen recordings?
faq.answer: Use software like OBS Studio, which includes a toggle to hide the cursor during your recording.

faq.question: What is the best way to hide the cursor manually?
faq.answer: Move the cursor to the edge of your display or off-screen if you use multiple monitors.

faq.question: Does Cursorcerer work on modern macOS?
faq.answer: Yes, versions like 4.1 support modern releases such as Sequoia and Tahoe.

task: Hide the cursor while working in Pages

steps.name: Move the cursor manually
steps.text: Move your mouse cursor to the extreme edge of your display. If you have a secondary monitor, move the cursor off the side of the main screen.

steps.name: Use a third-party utility
steps.text: Download and install a tool like Cursorcerer. Open the app and set your preferred global hotkey for toggling the cursor visibility.

steps.name: Toggle the cursor
steps.text: Press your chosen keyboard shortcut (default ⌃ ⌥ K) to hide the cursor while you are working in Pages.

troubleshooting.problem: Cursor does not disappear when using a shortcut.
troubleshooting.fix: Check if the third-party app has the necessary accessibility permissions in System Settings.

troubleshooting.problem: I lost my cursor and cannot find it.
troubleshooting.fix: Move your mouse or press your toggle key to bring it back. Enable the show on move setting.
